name: PowerShell
summary: Object-pipeline shell and scripting language from Microsoft built on .NET: cmdlets pass typed .NET objects (not text) through pipelines, with optional type constraints, script blocks, classes and a large cmdlet library; cross-platform and open source since PowerShell Core 6.

level_notes.1: The Windows PowerShell Language Specification 3.0 (republished on learn.microsoft.com) is the only formal spec and predates later features (classes, ternary, null-conditional, pipeline-chain operators); for those the about_* help topics and accepted PowerShell RFCs are the normative descriptions.
level_notes.0: PowerShell/PowerShell (C#, MIT licence) is the de facto definition; the language engine is in src/System.Management.Automation/engine (parser/, runtime/, interpreter/). Pash was an abandoned open-source reimplementation.
